data.title: SCB denies Tawan-Oil Trading ever held account with bank
data.description: Siam Commercial Bank says Tawan-Oil Trading has never held an account, conducted transactions or had a business relationship with the bank.

data.title: 'The Human Idea' offering cash prizes for bright sparks
data.description: Leading property developer AP Thailand and Adapter Digital invite creative thinkers and university students to join "The Human Idea – Creative Sprint 2026" to vie for cash prizes worth over 1.2 million baht.

data.title: Your daily horoscope for Oct 27
data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on. ✨= today's motto,⏰ = work, ₿ = money, ❤️= taken, ⚤ = single

data.title: Rethinking relief food
data.description: Last November, Hat Yai woke up to water. Heavy downpours for multiple days and flash floods submerged Songkhla and other southern provinces. Some managed to evacuate in time, while others were left stranded.

data.title: Makeup as an object to wear
data.description: Since her appointment in 2024, Sarah Burton has been shaping a vision of Givenchy that brings luxury closer to everyday life. Her latest collection extends jewellery beyond the usual mediums, turning beauty products into fashion accessories in their own right.

data.title: Sala Sudasiri Sobha hosts Duo Baraldi from Italy
data.description: OLive Music presents "Roots And Migrations" by Duo Baraldi from Italy at Sala Sudasiri Sobha, Lat Phrao 41 yaek 7-2, on Sunday at 4pm.

data.title: Oktoberfest comes to  One Bangkok Park
data.description: One Bangkok invites everyone to join "One Oktoberfest", a grand celebration inspired by Germany's iconic cultural festival at One Bangkok Park, Rama IV Road, from tomorrow to Sunday, starting from 4pm on weekdays and 2pm on weekends.

data.title: Trail venue boundaries come under scrutiny
data.description: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) is investigating whether a trail running venue in Nakhon Nayok's Ban Na district extends beyond its permitted boundaries or encroaches on state land.

data.title: Courts review sentencing rules for major offences
data.description: The Courts of Justice are setting up five subcommittees to review sentencing guidelines for major offences, including drug, technology, election, traffic, firearms, corruption and environmental crimes.

data.title: Dust-free rooms for at-risk groups
data.description: The government plans to establish 234 dust-free rooms for 6,077 vulnerable people in northern Thailand by next year to protect them from PM2.5 pollution, deputy government spokeswoman Patdarasm Thongsaluaykorn said.

data.title: Port have a mountain to climb in Johor
data.description: Port travel to Malaysia today seeking their first points of this season's AFC Champions League Elite, facing domestic powerhouse Johor Darul Ta'zim at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium (5pm Thai time).

data.title: Aimsaard sisters quit BAT, go solo
data.description: Women's doubles badminton players Nuntakarn Aimsaard and Benyapa Aimsaard have announced their decision to part ways with the Badminton Association of Thailand (BAT) to pursue their careers as independent athletes.

data.title: Senate approves Supreme Court judge for audit panel
data.description: The Senate approved Supreme Court judge Kajondej Janwattananon as a member of the State Audit Commission (SAC) in a 143-0 vote.

data.title: Lula win rattles Brazil markets over spending spree fears
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - The reelection of Brazilian leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva rattled markets on Monday as investors, who had expected a win for his conservative rival, worried about fiscal discipline.

data.title: Sophon says censure will go ahead
data.description: House Speaker Sophon Zarum said a no-confidence debate would take place before the current parliamentary session ends, but the government and opposition remain at odds over the schedule.

data.title: BMA seeks over B1bn in extra relief
data.description: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) plans to seek more than 1 billion baht in additional flood relief funding and has ordered district chiefs to draw up a new flood risk map following the capital's recent inundation.

data.title: Royals set to  see requiem  performance
data.description: Their Majesties the King and Queen will preside over and attend the premiere of "A Royal Requiem: Music in Memory and Prayers" on Nov 18 at Assumption Cathedral in Bangkok, an event organised by the Apostolic Nunciature of the Holy See in Thailand and the Catholic Bishops' Conference of Thailand (CBCT).

data.title: Elders council opposes end to sin tax earmarks
data.description: The Senior Citizens Council of Thailand has opposed proposed amendments to four sin tax laws that would end direct allocations of alcohol and tobacco excise revenue to public organisations and funds.

data.title: PM tells City Hall to clarify use of funds
data.description: Bangkok has spent 372 million baht of its 400-million-baht emergency budget on flood relief, including a 210-million-baht transfer to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) for household compensation, Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Monday.

data.title: DSI asked to probe border projects
data.description: Political activist Sonthiya Sawaddee has petitioned the Department of Special Investigation (DSI) to audit the funding and approvals for three border projects run by the Gun Jompalang Chuai Su Foundation near Cambodia.

data.title: PM says airport rail link contract remains binding
data.description: The high-speed rail link connecting three airports must proceed under the existing contract, and any unresolved disputes would face legal proceedings, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Monday.

data.title: Ministry faces shortage  of doctor posts by 2029
data.description: The Public Health Ministry could run out of civil-service doctor posts by 2029, leaving a projected 5,442 new doctors without such positions by 2040 unless the staffing ceiling is expanded, a Mahidol University study has found.

data.title: Trade and peace top talks agenda
data.description: Malaysian Foreign Minister Dato' Seri Utama Haji Mohamad bin Haji Hasan begins a two-day visit to Thailand on Tuesday for talks on bilateral cooperation, security and border development.

data.title: Anutin eases fears over holy basil rights protection
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has assured the public that protection rights for four varieties of holy basil will not prevent people from growing the herb for consumption or sale.

data.title: Thaksin amnesty petition awaits review
data.description: Justice permanent secretary Piyasiri Wattanawarangkun said a subcommittee he chairs had yet to receive former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra's request for amnesty in political cases.

data.title: Brazilian lawmaker Andre Janones, Lula's social media 'general'
data.description: SAO PAULO - In Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's first victory speech, he praised "our general" Andre Janones, the brains behind the online campaign that ensured his stunning comeback.

data.title: Netanyahu, rivals trade attacks over Iran as clock counts down to Israel vote
data.description: JERUSALEM - Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wrapped up his campaign to remain in power on Monday with a claim that Israel faced potential annihilation at the hands of Iran should his election rivals prevail.

data.title: Canadian youth seek climate action in landmark trial
data.description: VANCOUVER - Fifteen young Canadians will try to prove their nation's federal government has breached their rights through insufficient action on climate change in a landmark trial that has opened in the west coast city of Vancouver.

data.title: Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
data.description: PORT HURON — US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a "shit house country," and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize.

data.title: Part of London's Oxford Street pedestrianised 'forever'
data.description: LONDON - A stretch of London's iconic Oxford Street was made traffic-free "forever" starting Monday, as pedestrians took over the country's most famous shopping street, absent of the capital's red double-decker buses and black cabs.

data.title: Kane tipped to beat Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d'Or glory
data.description: LONDON - Harry Kane has been called the favourite to become England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years when the award is presented in London on Monday, but he faces stiff competition from La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

data.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
data.description: RIYADH — Yemen's Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.

data.title: Russia says open to lesser ceasefires with Ukraine, not end of war
data.description: MOSCOW - Russia said Monday that it would not slow down its offensive on Ukraine despite upcoming US-brokered talks on ending the conflict but that it could agree local "humanitarian" ceasefires.

data.title: Swedish Centre Party leader says government coalition talks failed
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Swedish Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist on Monday said she had failed to form a government uniting left and right wing parties, leaving the Nordic country no closer to a new government after its September 13 election.
